### Exercise 2: Building the request in R

We will now build the request in R using `httr2`.

Start with the base URL:

```{r}
#| eval: false

request("https://api.worldbank.org")
```

**(a)** Add the path to the request.

```{r}
#| eval: false

request("https://api.worldbank.org") |>
  YOUR_CODE
```

**(b)** Add the query parameters so that we request the 2020 observation in JSON format.

```{r}
#| eval: false

request("https://api.worldbank.org") |>
  YOUR_CODE |>
  YOUR_CODE
```

**(c)** Send the request to the World Bank API and save the response as `response`.

```{r}
#| eval: false
response <-
  request("https://api.worldbank.org") |>
  YOUR_CODE |>
  YOUR_CODE |>
  YOUR_CODE
```

**(d)** In your own words, explain what each of the following functions does in the request:

- `request()`
- `req_url_path_append()`
- `req_url_query()`
- `req_perform()`

::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.teaching-block}

::: {.teaching-block-header}
Teaching Note
:::

::: {.teaching-block-body}

🎯 **Learning Objective**

Students should:

- translate the parts of an API URL into an `httr2` request;
- use `request()`, `req_url_path_append()`, `req_url_query()`, and `req_perform()` to build and send an API request;
- explain the role of each function in the request.

✅ **Core Concepts to Highlight**

- `request()` starts the request with the API's base URL.
- `req_url_path_append()` adds the path that identifies the resource we want.
- `req_url_query()` adds query parameters that further specify the request.
- `req_perform()` sends the request to the API.
- The code mirrors the URL structure from Exercise 1: base URL, path, then query parameters.

💬 **Suggested In-Class Prompts**

- Which part of the code would we change if we wanted a different year?
- Which part would we change if we wanted a different indicator?
- What would happen if we built the request but did not call `req_perform()`?

📌 **Common Misunderstandings**

- Putting the full path inside a single character string rather than passing the path components to `req_url_path_append()`.
- Including `?` or `&` inside `req_url_query()`.
- Forgetting that `req_perform()` is the step that actually sends the request.
- Treating `request()` as if it downloads the data immediately.

:::

:::

:::

<!-- BEGIN PROFILE:r-solutions -->
::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-solutions" when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.solution-block}

::: {.solution-block-header}
Solution
:::

::: {.solution-block-body}

(a) Add the path using `req_url_path_append()`.

```{r}
request("https://api.worldbank.org") |>
  req_url_path_append(
    "v2",
    "country",
    "AUS",
    "indicator",
    "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
  )
```

(b) Add the query parameters using `req_url_query()`.

```{r}
request("https://api.worldbank.org") |>
  req_url_path_append(
    "v2",
    "country",
    "AUS",
    "indicator",
    "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
  ) |>
  req_url_query(
    date = 2020,
    format = "json"
  )
```

(c) Send the request using `req_perform()` and save the response.

```{r}
response <-
  request("https://api.worldbank.org") |>
  req_url_path_append(
    "v2",
    "country",
    "AUS",
    "indicator",
    "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
  ) |>
  req_url_query(
    date = 2020,
    format = "json"
  ) |>
  req_perform()
```

(d)

- `request()` starts a new request using the World Bank API's base URL.
- `req_url_path_append()` adds the path that identifies the country and indicator we want.
- `req_url_query()` adds the year and asks the API to return the response in JSON format.
- `req_perform()` sends the request to the API and returns the response.

:::

:::
